title: Minority children at risk from ETS.
ehr_evidence: The study measured four biomarkers in the blood cells of 109 Hispanic and African-American children, ages 1 to 6 (cotinine, two carcinogenic protein complexes, and sister chromatid exchanges).
summary: A cross-sectional study measuring four blood-cell biomarkers in 109 Hispanic and African-American children ages 1 to 6 to assess genetic damage associated with environmental tobacco smoke (ETS) exposure.
key_findings: The four biomarkers increased with ETS exposure across all exposure groups (no ETS, ETS from a household member other than the mother, and ETS via maternal smoking).
population: 109 Hispanic and African-American children, ages 1 to 6
limitations: Small sample size (N=109) and reliance on a single news summary rather than the primary study data, limiting quantitative detail such as effect sizes and p-values.
